title: In vivo Imaging of Biological Tissues with Combined Two-Photon Fluorescence and Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
protocol: Use an integrated optical parametric oscillator (OPO) connected with a mode-locked Ytterbium fiber laser as the ps laser source for SRS imaging.
Collimate and adjust the size of the fs beam to 3 mm using lenses L1 and L2.
Collimate the ps laser beam and expand its diameter to 3 mm using lenses L3 and L4.
Change the polarization of the fs laser beam from p polarization to s polarization using a half-wave plate.
Combine the two laser beams with a polarizing beam splitter (PBS).
Add a pair of 3 mm XY-scan galvanometer mirrors behind the PBS for beam scanning.
Use a telecentric scan lens (L5) and an infinity-corrected tube lens (L6).
Expand the laser beam with the scan lens and tube lens to fill the back aperture of the objective.
Place a PBS or dichroic mirror (D2) between the tube lens and objective lens for SRS or fluorescence signal collection.
Use a motorized flipper to switch between PBS and D2.
Narrow the detection beam using lenses (L7 and L9).
Conjugate the rear pupil of the 25x objective lens with a photodiode sensor using lenses (L7 and L9).
Narrow the detection beam using lenses (L8 and L10).
Conjugate the rear pupil of the 25x objective with the detection surface of the photomultiplier (PMT) using lenses (L8 and L10).
Use a dichroic mirror (D3) to separate the detection path of fluorescence and SRS signals.
Place a filter set (Fs1) in front of the photodiode detector to block the Stokes laser and pass the pump beam only.
Place a filter set (Fs2) in front of the PMT detector to pass the target fluorescence signal only.
Connect the PMT to a current amplifier for signal amplification.
Connect the photodiode to a lock-in amplifier.
Connect the sync signal from the built-in EOM output to the reference input of the lock-in amplifier for SRS signal demodulation.
Connect the PMT amplifier and lock-in amplifier outputs to the data acquisition module.
Switch the key switch from Standby to On position to turn on the Ti: sapphire laser.
Wait for 30 min for the Ti: sapphire laser to warm up.
Click on the Start button on the OPO control panel to switch on the OPO.
Wait for 20 min for the OPO laser to warm up.
Open the laser shutter for the Stokes beam.
Place a high-speed photodetector at the OPO output.
Connect the output port of the photodetector to an oscilloscope using a coaxial cable with BNC connector.
Adjust the EOM power and phase according to the pulse intensity diagram shown on the oscilloscope to achieve maximal modulation depth at 20 MHz.
Perform optical alignment for colocalization of the ps and fs beams as described in steps 2.2.2 to 2.2.13.
Open the pump laser shutter while stopping the Stokes output in the OPO control software.
Set the wavelength of the pump beam to 796 nm using the Set Signal box and entering 796.
Set the power of the pump beam to the minimum (~20 mW) for optical alignment by clicking on the Set OPO Power box and entering 20.
Switch on the microscope computer and all associated electronic components, including scanners, objective actuators, photodiodes, PMTs, current amplifiers, lock-in amplifiers, and motorized flippers.
Start the microscope control software.
Place two alignment plates (P1 and P2) on the optical path behind PBS and P1 respectively at distances of about 10 cm and 30 cm from PBS.
Open the microscope shutter for the ps laser beam.
Adjust mirror M1 to locate the ps laser beam center at the through-hole of P1 using an infrared scope.
Adjust mirror M2 to locate the ps laser beam center at the through-hole of P2 using an infrared scope.
Close the shutter of the ps beam in the microscope control software.
Set the wavelength of fs Ti: sapphire laser at 740 nm and open the laser shutter.
Set the laser power to 5 mW (measured at the input port of the microscope system) for optical alignment.
Open the microscope shutter for the fs laser beam.
Adjust the mirror M3 to locate the fs laser beam spot center at the through-hole of P1.
Adjust the mirror M4 to locate the laser beam spot center at the through-hole of P2.
Place an alignment plate P0 before L3.
Adjust the optical mirror 1 (OM1) using a hex key so that the Stokes beam center passes through the through-hole of the alignment plate and colocalizes with the pump beam at the laser output port.
Confirm the position of the beam spot at P0 during adjustment using an IR scope.
Remove the alignment plate P0.
Adjust the optical mirror 2 (OM2) using a hex key so that the center of the Stokes beam colocalizes with the reference mark of the pump beam on the camera.
Repeat steps to ensure the Stokes beam strictly overlaps with the pump beam at both P0 and camera planes.
Optimize imaging conditions by performing phase adjustment of the lock-in amplifier as described in specific steps.
Set the wavelength of the pump laser to 796 nm.
Set the power of the pump and Stokes beams to 15 mW and 25 mW on the sample, respectively.
Seal olive oil in a slide for SRS imaging optimization and calibration.
Attach a folded tissue paper to the bottom of the slide to enhance signal backscattering for epi-SRS detection.
Place the olive oil sample on the stage.
Adjust the focus of the 25x objective onto the sample.
Set the imaging parameters using microscope control software: 512 x 512 pixels for a 500 μm x 500 μm field of view, 6.4 μs pixel dwell time.
Set the time constant value to 10 μs in lock-in amplifier control software.
Scan the laser beam over the sample.
Tune the phase (0-180°) using lock-in amplifier control software with a step size of 22.5° until SRS signal intensity reaches maximum.
Scan the sample with laser shutter closed.
Tune the offset value using lock-in amplifier control software until the average SRS signal is close to zero.
Use a step size of 1 mV for tuning.
Perform temporal synchronization optimization as described in steps 2.3.9 to 2.3.14.
Open the Delay Manager dialogue in the OPO control software.
Scan the olive oil and tune the delay stage until the olive oil SRS signal reaches its maximum.
Stop scanning and click on the Add Data button in the delay manager dialogue to record current delay data.
Repeat steps 2.3.10 and 2.3.11 for different chemical samples at different wavelengths.
Sterilize all required tools, including scalpels, spring scissors, forceps, coverslips, and gauze pads.
Disinfect all surfaces that would be touched during surgery with 70% ethanol.
Cover the working area of the benchtop with sterile drapes.
Place a heating pad under the drape.
Use Thy1-YFP-H transgenic mice for in vivo spinal cord imaging.
Weigh the mouse and induce anesthesia by intraperitoneal injection of ketamine-xylazine mixture (87.5 mg kg-1 and 12.5 mg kg-1).
Pinch the toe of the mouse to ensure deep anesthesia.
Supplement with half the original dose of anesthetics if needed.
Apply ointment to the mouse eyes to prevent corneal dryness.
Shave the hair on the back above the thoracic spine.
Remove the hair using depilating cream.
Disinfect the shaved area with iodine solution.
Make a small midline incision (~1.5 cm) over the T11-T13 vertebra with a scalpel.
Incise muscles and tendons both on top and on sides of the T11-T13 vertebra with spring scissors and forceps.
Expose the three adjacent vertebras.
Use sterile gauze pads and sterile saline to control bleeding and clean the surgical site.
Stabilize the spine with the help of two stainless steel sidebars on a custom-designed stabilization stage.
Perform a laminectomy at T12 using a #2 forcep.
Carefully break the lamina piece by piece until the whole lamina of the T12 vertebra is removed.
Wash away the blood overlying the spinal cord with sterile saline.
Absorb excessive fluid with a gauze pad.
Apply pressure on the bleeding site with a piece of gauze pad to control bleeding.
Place a coverslip (22 x 22 mm) on the clamping bar.
Fill the interspace between the coverslip and the spinal cord with saline.
Mount the stabilization stage on a five-axis stage beneath the TPEF-SRS microscope.
Secure the mouse head with two head bars.
Lower the holding plate to offer enough space for chest movement during breathing.
Insert a heating pad under the mouse to keep it warm during imaging.
Adjust the z translational stage to tune the focus until the bright-field image of spinal cord vasculature can be observed under a 10x objective.
Locate the spinal cord dorsal vein at the center of the FOV by tuning the two-axis translational stage of the five-axis stage.
Tune the roll and pitch angles of the five-axis stage to adjust the spinal cord dorsal surface perpendicular to the objective axis based on the bright-field image.
Replace the 10x with a 25x water immersion objective for TPEF-SRS imaging.
Set the wavelength of the fs beam to 920 nm.
Tune the fs beam power to be 10 mW on the sample.
Set the wavelength of the pump beam to 796 nm.
Tune the power of the pump and Stokes beam to be 60 mW and 75 mW on the sample, respectively.
Select PBS above the objective using a motorized flipper by pressing the Switch button connected to the motorized flipper.
Set the imaging parameters as follows: 512 x 512 pixels for 150 μm x 150 μm FOV.
Set the pixel dwell time to 3.2 μs.
Set the time constant to 2 μs.
Start scanning the sample and set the focus on the dorsal surface of the spinal cord.
Finely tune the delay stage by the OPO control software until maximum spinal cord SRS signal is achieved.
Select dichroic mirror D2 above the objective using a motorized flipper by pressing the Switch button connected to the motorized flipper.
Set the imaging parameters and start scanning the sample.
Acquire the TPEF and SRS images sequentially with a 1 s interval at the same depth before going to the next depth.
Capture the TPEF-SRS image stack using imaging parameters of 512 x 512 pixels, 150 μm x 150 μm FOV, and 3.2 μs pixel dwell time.
Remove the animal from the stabilization stage after all images are collected.
Clean the exposed tissue by flushing with saline.
Absorb excess fluid using a gauze pad.
Apply silicone gel on the exposed spinal cord.
Wait for approximately 5 minutes until the silicone gel gets cured.
Suture the skin with #6-0 surgical suture to close the wound.
Apply burn cream on the skin of the surgical site to prevent infection.
Administer analgesic treatment subcutaneously (0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine).
Place the animal in a clean cage and place the cage on a heating pad until the mouse fully recovers from anesthesia.
Repeat analgesic administration every 12 hours for 3 days after surgery.
Set the power of the pump and Stokes beam to the maximum.
Set the wavelength of the pump beam and fs laser to 800 nm.
Set the two lasers on standby.
